title: Prefix values determined by linear checks
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a Boolean vector of length $2m$, and let $P$ be a Boolean proof string indexed by $m+(m+1)$ positions. Suppose every linear check holds for every seed, where the checks include the endpoint values, the products of paired input bits, and the successive-prefix recurrence. Then, for every $k$ with $0\le k\le m$, the bit of $P$ at prefix index $k$, interpreted in $\mathbb{F}_2$, equals the sum in $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the products of the first $k$ paired input bits.
hypotheses_covered: $w$ is a Boolean vector of length $2m$
$P$ is a Boolean vector of length $m+(m+1)$
Every linear check holds for every seed
